stated: The Conservative Party will complete the process of leasehold reform, capping ground rents at £250 (reducing to peppercorn over time), ending misuse of forfeiture, and making commonhold easier to adopt.

source.quote: We will complete the process of leasehold reform, to improve the lives of over four million leaseholders. We will cap ground rents at £250, reducing them to peppercorn over time. We will end the misuse of forfeiture so leaseholders don’t lose their property and capital unfairly and make it easier to take up commonhold.

bearing_set.reason: Ground rent caps directly reduce the recurring cost burden on leaseholders, ending forfeiture misuse protects security of tenure, and commonhold reform alters the ownership structure — all core O1 indicators (affordability, tenure security, ownership conditions).

Forfeiture is a mechanism by which landlords can seize a property worth hundreds of thousands of pounds for minor breaches — ending its misuse is a direct protection of property rights against arbitrary interference (an explicit O10 indicator); making commonhold easier expands owners' autonomy over their buildings, reducing ongoing landlord coercion.

membership_note: The policy bears on O1 (housing affordability/security of tenure) as its primary home for the cost and security effects, and on O10 (property rights/freedom from coercion) via forfeiture protection and commonhold expansion. O2 could be argued for the bills-reduction aspect of ground rent caps, but ground rents are housing rents — the O1 'rent as % of income' indicator is the precise home. No public-finance or inequality bearing is large enough to clear the non-negligible bar for O12 or O14.
